Audit an existing feature for where it breaks on odd input, state or sequence; findings only, read-only on the repo unless the owner asked for fixes.

1. Name the flows and, per flow, the promises to break: inputs (empty, huge, Unicode and Korean, quotes, time zones), states (first run, retry, restart, concurrent use) and links to other systems.
2. Real surface: with `.omp/skills/verify-<app>/`, the UI worker launches an isolated instance through it and drives the UI there. Without one, write "UI not driven: no verify skill" in the report; do not build one inside the audit.
3. Main reads code and writes briefs; workers run every probe, for a single flow too. Only a target of one small file with no UI may be probed by main, after main reads that kind's `Read first:` skill itself. Split by kind of probe (input boundary, UI, ordering) only on HEAVY work: there, one worker per flow and kind. On LIGHT work, one worker per flow covers input and ordering, and a flow with a UI adds one UI worker. A brief names at most about 10 source files and opens with a `Read first:` line naming the skill of each kind it covers: input boundaries and LIGHT ordering `skill://pbt`; a UI flow on the verify instance `skill://bombadil` and the verify skill; ordering or retry flows on HEAVY work `skill://statechart`. Each brief carries the contract: "a finding counts only with its command and captured output; no output, no finding". A UI brief also requires one bombadil run against the verify instance, its output saved with the probes, or the error that stopped it.
4. Probes (scripts, property tests, bombadil specs, captures) go to `~/.omp/agent/audits/<repo>/<date>-<slug>/`, never `/tmp`, so a later fix reuses them as its red test.
5. Rerun the command of every finding you will report and drop what does not reproduce. Review seats (`skill://interrogate`) only on HEAVY work or the owner's request.
6. A confirmed defect routes to `playbooks/bug-fix.md` with its probe as the red test; start fixing only when the owner asked for fixes.

Reply, in Korean plain text: each finding with its command and the output it printed, the probes path, and what was not driven (surfaces, flows, inputs).
